name: workshop-apply-earns-a-real-verdict
description:
The first bronze bundle that proves something about the BUILDER itself rather than the harness: that its author->apply->read-the-verdict loop runs against a REAL reconciler, and that a genuine cross-build-space refusal reaches a real tool result.

The scripted session calls `workshop_apply` (pkg/tools/workshopmcp/tools_apply.go's handleApply, mounted for real by test/e2e/workshop_mcp.go's mountWorkshopMCP -- see workshop-inventory-is-real's bundle for the same real-server-vs-canned-stub explanation) TWICE, applying two different candidate AgentClass manifests into the workshop's own namespace, and reads back applyCR's polled status.conditions from each tool result -- the REAL pkg/controllers/agentclass reconciler's own verdict, not a canned reply:

  1. `builder-candidate-foreign` references a SpiceboxToolspec (`ts-foreign-workshop`) labeled `agentprimitives.authzed.com/workshop-namespace: other-build-space` -- a DIFFERENT namespace than the one this candidate actually lands in ("default"). pkg/controllers/agentclass/builderclass.go's validateBuilderClass (called from controller.go's Reconcile, the CONSUMER half of the workshop's prefix/label rule -- see that function's own doc) refuses it: Valid=False, reason=ReferencesWorkshopTool.
  2. `builder-candidate-clean` references `ts-own-workshop` -- a sibling toolspec labeled for `default`, the namespace the candidate actually lands in. Same reconciler, same namespace, same identityMode, same toolBundles SHAPE: the two candidates differ in exactly one VALUE, the toolspec's workshop-namespace label. Valid=True. That is what makes the pair pin the LABEL as the discriminator rather than merely the presence of a toolspec reference -- a regression refusing ANY toolspec ref would pass a pair whose clean half carried none.

One refusal alone would only prove the gate can fire; asserting BOTH from the SAME bundle is what proves the loop DISCRIMINATES rather than always refusing (or always allowing) whatever a builder proposes. Both assertions are on `lastToolResultContains` against the tool result's JSON (`applyCR`'s serialized `status.conditions`), never on the agent's prose -- a scripted transcript would say the same words either way. (The bundle's own `assert.agentReplyContains` check on "ReferencesWorkshopTool" IS on prose -- it is the required blocking assertion every bronze bundle needs so the run cannot race ahead of the pipeline, not a claim about authorization semantics; the two `lastToolResultContains` checks above carry the actual claims.)

Ordering note: pkg/controllers/agentclass's validateBundles runs BEFORE validateBuilderClass in Reconcile, and requires every toolBundles[].toolspecs entry to itself be Valid=True (or the class fails there instead, for the wrong reason). `ts-foreign-workshop` is pre-stamped Valid=True by the driver's stampToolspecsValid stand-in (this harness runs no real SpiceboxToolspec controller) before the scripted turns run, so the foreign-labeled toolspec's own validity is never in question -- only its label is.

WHAT THIS BUNDLE DOES NOT PROVE: the ADMISSION-side half of the same workshop prefix/label rule (a validating webhook refusing the write outright, before it ever reaches a reconciler) is NOT exercised here. This harness registers no validating admission webhook at all -- a bundle asserting "the webhook refused" would assert nothing, because the write would simply succeed, and it would be indistinguishable in CI from the same bundle run against a cluster where a real webhook refusal happened. This bundle instead asserts on the CONSUMER-side gate (validateBuilderClass), which IS wired in this harness. A green run here is evidence the consumer gate discriminates correctly; it must NOT be read as evidence the admission-side lockdown is registered or exercised anywhere in this suite.
userTurns: I have two candidate agent classes to propose: one that references a tool from a different build space, and a clean one with no such reference. Apply both and tell me what the real controller says about each.

args._reason: apply the first candidate -- it references a toolspec labeled for a different build space, and I want to see whether the real controller refuses it

spec.description: Candidate class referencing a toolspec labeled for a different build space.

systemPrompt.inline: placeholder system prompt for a candidate class under test

args._reason: the foreign-labeled candidate was refused as expected; now apply the clean candidate, which references no workshop tool at all

spec.description: Candidate class referencing a toolspec labeled for its OWN build space -- identical in shape to the refused candidate, differing only in that label.

systemPrompt.inline: placeholder system prompt for a candidate class under test

reply.text: The foreign-labeled candidate was refused by the real controller (Valid=False, reason ReferencesWorkshopTool). The clean candidate, otherwise identical, reconciled Valid=True. The controller discriminates on the reference, not just on the shape of the request.

args.summary: applied a foreign-referencing candidate (refused, ReferencesWorkshopTool) and a clean candidate (accepted) and reported the real controller's verdict on each
